subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Flywheels: Storing Energy in Spin
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Flywheels: Storing Energy in Spin.

hook.text: A potter's wheel keeps spinning between kicks. That's a flywheel — storing energy as rotational momentum.

buildup.text: A flywheel's energy depends on mass and speed squared. Double the spin rate and you store four times the energy.

discovery.text: Engine flywheels smooth out power delivery. Each piston fires briefly, but the flywheel keeps the crankshaft spinning.

twist.text: Modern flywheel batteries spin carbon fiber rotors at 60,000 rpm in a vacuum. They charge and discharge instantly.

climax.text: Formula 1 used KERS flywheels — braking stored energy that drivers released as a power boost on straights.

punchline.text: Spin something heavy. Energy stays until you need it.

quiz.question: Why does doubling a flywheel's spin rate quadruple its stored energy?
options: Faster spin creates more friction that converts to stored heat energy
Rotational energy depends on speed squared, so double speed means four times the energy
The centrifugal force compresses the flywheel, storing elastic energy
